title: Sacred Thieves
text: “If I’m being honest, I never thought I’d be capable of handling slaves like this… but I figured the situation was just too awful to ignore.”
Father glanced furtively over at the mixed-breed Lizardmen.
“Motoyasu-kun told me I should teach the slaves to smile while defeating monsters, and I remember thinking, what kind of monster does that make future-me?”
“So how’s it actually turned out?”
“Well… it’s a bit easier since Shion and the others are male. Still questionable, I know, but they’re putting on this circus act and at least they seem motivated, so that helps.”
“Well, judging by that exchange just now, it doesn’t look like you’re forcing them to work, so I’d say it’s fine.”

By the way, Father was properly paying his slaves wages, I say. The mixed-breed Lizardmen received money to buy what they needed, but always returned the change untouched. Wolf, meanwhile, didn’t really grasp the concept of spending wages at all, so he just handed the whole amount straight back.
“Sounds exactly like something you’d do, Little Bro. So, what about equipment?”
“That, indeed. Father, I think it’d be best to have him make you a set of barbarian armor.”

That trademark armor of Father’s, indeed. That would suit him perfectly. As for my own equipment, I’d already crafted it myself, so there was no issue there. So long as I gathered molted feathers from Filolial-sama, I could produce it anytime, I say.
“You sure know a lot, don’t you? That fine with you?”
“Of course, indeed. I already know exactly what materials are needed.”
I pulled the materials out of my spear one after another and handed them over.
“Makes me want to ask where the heck that stuff keeps coming from, but I guess that’s just heroes for you.”
“Everything just gets chalked up to ‘heroes,’ huh.”

HAHAHA, if it’s something Father wants, I’ll handle just about anything, I say. By the way, I’d already taught Father Weapon Copy, so between us we’d covered a considerable number of shields across Zeltoble, indeed.
“Also, I happen to know this weapon shop has a meteoric iron shield, so I’d like to take a look at it later, I say.”
“Seriously, is there anything you don’t know?”
“And after that, let’s talk a bit in the back of the shop, indeed.”

From here on, just as we’d done back when we stayed in Melromarc, we arranged to hand over the drop items to the weapon shop owner and have him skillfully funnel them into equipment for us. The negotiations went smoothly. After that, we got the slaves properly equipped, all while staying within bounds that wouldn’t raise the Three Heroes Church’s suspicions. As for equipment for the Filolial-sama? That fell under the monster merchant’s jurisdiction apparently, so the order got placed right away. In the loop where we’d stayed in Melromarc, Sakura-chan had mainly gone with her angel form and dual-wielded, but Filo-tan was still an egg this time, so I hadn’t prepared any weapon for her yet. And as for the Filolial-sama joining this wave, there weren’t really that many who preferred using human-made weapons anyway.
“Well then, guess we’ll rush and prioritize Little Bro’s armor first? As for the rest… well, I’ll get all sorts of things ready for you.”

The weapon shop owner, looking somewhat wry, agreed to disguise the bribe weapons I’d handed him and pass them off appropriately. The mixed-breed Lizardman apparently decided on an axe. The Rabbit man asked for a staff, planning to use the magic he’d learned, but apparently the Lizardman told him to carry a dagger too, just in case.
For now, we’d placed whatever orders could be handled at the weapon shop.
“Well, good luck out there, you lot! I’m rooting for you.”
“Yeah. See you another day, then.”
And with that, we left the weapon shop, indeed.
“He seemed like quite a decent fellow, didn’t he.”
“The selection and quality of the weapons weren’t bad either.”
“Yeah. I think he’s a good person.”
Father agreed with the slaves’ impressions, indeed.
“Kuro’s gonna use a sword, huh~”
“One shouldn’t attempt what one isn’t used to, you know.”
“Hmm…”
And so, a few days later, Father tried on that familiar barbarian armor.
“Hmm… quite fitting, actually. Everyone seems to like that rugged, wild look.”
“It suits you very well.”
“Waaargh!”
The slaves each praised Father’s appearance in their own way.
“I’m a little curious why Shion’s talking to me like I’m a child, but… well, I guess this is just how it is.”
“That barbarian armor suits you well, doesn’t it.”
“About this ‘barbarian’ thing…”
“Ah, in this country it refers to demi-humans and beastmen, you know? Since you’re the Shield Hero, Little Bro, leaning that direction tends to go over better, don’t you think?”

At the weapon shop owner’s reply, the slaves all nodded in unison. So it really was, by their peculiar sense of style, an armor design they genuinely thought suited him. As expected, whenever Father wore this armor, even I found myself switching into battle-mode awareness. Everyone took their newly crafted weapons in hand.
“Well then, good luck out there, you lot.”
“Yeah. I’ll do my best. So I can live up to your expectations, old man.”
“Ha, I think that face suits you best, Little Bro. Don’t go getting too jaded — just get along well with everyone, alright?”

At the weapon shop owner’s words, I couldn’t help but think of Father back in my original world. It must have been rough for him. And yet, Big Sister had been there with him, so surely that eased his burden at least a little. I’d like to believe that, indeed.

Now then, the next stop was the Dragon Hourglass, indeed. Normally, the day we picked up Father’s armor was the same day we’d run into Ren and Itsuki, but by adjusting the schedule a bit, we could meet them today instead. And so, off we went to the facility. However, since the facility was managed by the Three Heroes Church’s people, we decided to leave Wolf waiting outside the building.
“Wolf, wait here.”
“Whine…”

Keel the dog had been allowed in before, but a wolfman like Wolf would surely be a stretch. It had already been made clear from the start that he wouldn’t be permitted inside important facilities, and since he’d only been granted permission to accompany us on this shopping trip under that condition, Wolf didn’t put up much of a fuss about it.
“Well… this might turn into a bit of a hassle, so both Shion and Theo, behave yourselves, alright?”
“Yeah.”
“Understood.”
Then Father turned to face me and Yuki-chan and the others.
“Ah… Motoyasu-kun, you’ll be fine, right?”
“Of course, indeed.”
The ones we were meeting here were Ren and Itsuki, after all. The Three Heroes Church lot were of so little concern to me as to barely register, indeed.
“Hey, Moto~ where’s the swordsman of darkness~?”
“You’ll get to meet him soon, indeed.”

Ren should be right here about now, after all. Best to let Kuro-chan take a look at him. She’d taken quite a liking to Ren and played with him before, indeed. And so, with that, we headed inside the building.
“B-Buoink!”
The moment we stepped in, a pig greeted us. Its squeal carried a rather sharp edge of anger.
“Huh? What is it?”
Father, playing the part, replied with a deliberately rough tone.
“B-Buh.”
The pig gave an awkward little cough, looking rather sheepish.
“Ah, right, apparently the wave’s tomorrow, so we came.”
Since the wave was drawing near, Father stated our business. But before leading us further, the pig squealed something else.
“Buh-buh-buh, buh-buh.”
“Why the hell do I have to talk about the bandits who attacked me?”
Apparently this pig from the Three Heroes Church had heard Father had been attacked by bandits, and was asking whether he’d been hurt, as well as what had happened to the bandits afterward.
“I don’t know a thing about what happened to any bandits.”
“Buh-buh-buh.”

The mixed-breed Lizardman and the Rabbit man watched the whole exchange with visibly displeased expressions, keeping dead silent. Apparently, stepping in wasn’t an option here. From what I heard afterward, the pig had apparently been cautioned about escorting the bandits to the proper authorities. That was it, wasn’t it. The pig couldn’t grasp the full truth of them being sold as slaves in Siltvelt, but sensed that some sort of processing was happening to them regardless. So, wanting to complain indirectly but unable to say so outright, it was warning him to hand the bandits over to the local watch instead. According to Father, apparently this pig’s own family — a sibling or parent, perhaps — had been one of the bandits who attacked him, gotten captured, and shipped off to Siltvelt, and the pig had been trying to voice a personal grievance about it within its limited means. Despite bringing the trouble entirely upon itself, it was still complaining. It seemed the Three Heroes Church was trying to spread rumors of a cannibal circus. But no matter which town the traveling circus visited, not a shred of evidence for that ever turned up, and Father’s circus was actually doing fairly well, all things considered. Since the show’s content was tailored to Melromarc’s tastes — a circus centered on abusing demi-humans and beastmen — there wasn’t much room to complain about the content itself.

“Why exactly am I being reprimanded here over some talk about criminal bandits? Don’t tell me — could it be that a follower claiming to be so ‘sacred’ was, by some mistake, actually one of the bandits?”
At Father’s provocation, the pig’s face twisted with fury.
“Buh-buh!”
“B-Buh, buh—”

At that point another pig cautioned the first one, so it gave another cough, and with an expression like it had bitten down on a sour bug, resumed leading us onward, indeed. By the way, we’d already confirmed the Dragon Hourglass over in Siltvelt, and Father had already mastered the Portal Skill by this point. I’d already relayed a fair amount about future events to him beforehand. This time around, he apparently intended to handle things carefully so as not to provoke Ren or Itsuki.
